hypothesis:
M1 tests whether DPO can calibrate the healthy selected M0-final-v2 policy without destroying its recovered calling capability. M0 already moved the policy from B0's over-calling frontier; this run is not authorized to increase call recall at any cost. It targets the frontier jointly: retain strong call recall and precision, reduce unnecessary calls, improve unsupported handling, and preserve clarification behavior. Tool selection and argument/schema validity remain explicit evaluation dimensions but are not promoted as measured until the evaluator computes them.
The student starts from the selected full-corpus M0-final-v2 checkpoint only. The DPO reference is an independently loaded copy of that same checkpoint, so this is calibration around the M0 policy rather than a return to the base model. The old base-starting DPO runs remain historical evidence and are not parents of this experiment.
Preference data is a frozen local calibration set: actual deterministic outputs from the pinned base and selected M0 on Canonical-v2 training prompts, retaining only cases where one output matches the canonical behavior decision, plus a bounded hash-ranked slice of curated When2Call preferences for clarification, unsupported and direct-answer behavior. Frozen DEV and confirmatory IDs are excluded before local generation. No paid external API was used.
